result.title: Against All Likelihood
result.summary: Maximum likelihood is the dominant training principle for large language models, yet likelihood is neither necessary nor sufficient for truth. Unlikely events happen every day, and frequently repeated statements can be false. Drawing on a philosophical tradition that ties objectivity to invariance rather than probability (from Nozick's account of objective facts and Wigner's principles of invariance to the structural realism of Poincaré and Cassirer), we argue that the truth of a statement should be judged not by its probability under a single distribution, but by its invariance across relevant transformations of the environment. We connect this view to machine learning literature on out-of-distribution generalization and invariant learning, sketch how invariance could be tested at inference time with language models, and discuss implications for continual learning.

AI.brief_summary: 这是一篇立场论文，论证最大似然既非真理的必要也非充分条件，主张以陈述在环境相关变换下是否保持不变（invariance）作为真理性判据，并联系 OOD 泛化与不变性学习文献，勾勒在推理期用语言模型检验不变性的思路及对持续学习的启示。
